Shared, lost and gained species between pairs of sites

Source: R/turnover-counts.R
beta_turnover_counts.Rd

For each pair of sites, beta_turnover_counts() counts the species they share, the species found only in the first site (lost on moving to the second) and only in the second (gained), and gives the pairwise dissimilarities with Baselga's partitions:

  • sorensen = turnover (Simpson dissimilarity, beta.sim) + nestedness (beta.sne) (Baselga 2010);

  • jaccard = turnover_j + nestedness_j (Baselga 2012);

  • with abundances, bray = balanced (balanced variation in abundance) + gradient (abundance gradient) (Baselga 2013).

The values equal those of the betapart package. Along a gradient, use pairs = "adjacent" with order_by to compare each site with the next.

A site with no species makes the dissimilarities undefined (0 / 0 when both sites are empty, or a pure loss): such pairs are returned with a warning, their counts are kept and undefined indices are NA.

Usage

beta_turnover_counts(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  pairs = "adjacent",
  order_by = NULL,
  .by = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

abundance

<tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

pairs

"adjacent" (each site with the next in order_by order), "all" (every pair), or a data frame with two columns of site names.

order_by

Column giving the order of sites for "adjacent" pairs, such as elevation; by default the natural site order.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

Value

A tibble with the grouping columns, site_1, site_2, s_1, s_2 (richness), shared, lost, gained, sorensen, turnover, nestedness, jaccard, turnover_j, nestedness_j, and with abundances bray, balanced and gradient.

References

Baselga, A. (2010). Partitioning the turnover and nestedness components of beta diversity. Global Ecology and Biogeography, 19, 134-143.

Baselga, A. (2012). The relationship between species replacement, dissimilarity derived from nestedness, and nestedness. Global Ecology and Biogeography, 21, 1223-1232.

Baselga, A. (2013). Separating the two components of abundance-based dissimilarity: balanced changes in abundance vs. abundance gradients. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 4, 552-557.

Examples

wet <- dplyr::filter(png_ants, season == "wet")
beta_turnover_counts(wet, abundance = workers, order_by = elevation)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 16
#>   site_1 site_2   s_1   s_2 shared  lost gained sorensen turnover nestedness
#>   <chr>  <chr>  <int> <int>  <int> <int>  <int>    <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 MW0200 MW0700    21    28      8    13     20    0.673    0.619     0.0544
#> 2 MW0700 MW1200    28    20      9    19     11    0.625    0.55      0.0750
#> 3 MW1200 MW1700    20    10      4    16      6    0.733    0.6       0.133 
#> 4 MW1700 MW2200    10     5      1     9      4    0.867    0.8       0.0667
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: jaccard <dbl>, turnover_j <dbl>, nestedness_j <dbl>,
#> #   bray <dbl>, balanced <dbl>, gradient <dbl>
